name: Akkas-Syria Gas Pipeline
monitor_reason: Fails add-threshold leg (c) concrete step (and arguably (a) sponsor). The Akkas-to-Syria/AGP gas EXPORT pipeline has no MOU, tender, FEED, EPC award, permit, or FID of its own — it exists only as a long-standing aspiration (2004 Egypt/Jordan/Syria/Lebanon framework to connect AGP to Iraq's grid; ~2009 Akkas–Europe-via-Türkiye concept) that stalled in the Syrian war / ISIS's 2014 seizure of Akkas, and is now only under 'renewed discussion' post-Assad. All concrete 2025-26 activity attaches to the Akkas FIELD (SLB drilling Jan 2026; Midland Oil Company lead; earlier Ukrzemresurs/KOGAS-Daewoo contracts), whose gas is targeted at domestic power generation, not a cross-border export line.
researcher_notes: Match-to-existing re-checked and ruled out: distinct from P0450 (Iran–Iraq–Syria/'Friendship', Iranian gas Asaluyeh→Damascus, cancelled), P1841 (Baiji-K3-Al Kaem, terminates at Al-Qa'im INSIDE Iraq, operating), and P7460/P7466/P7467 (Okaz–Al-Anbar, domestic Okaz-field feed to Anbar power plant, proposed). No existing GEM gas row captures an Akkas→Syria→AGP cross-border export link. However it does not clear the Discovery add-threshold. Add-threshold assessment: (a) sponsor — NOT identified for the pipeline itself (SLB/Midland Oil Company/Ukrzemresurs/KOGAS are Akkas FIELD operators, not pipeline sponsors); (b) endpoints — roughly present (Akkas, al-Anbar, ~30 km S of Al-Qa'im on the Syrian border → Syria → Arab Gas Pipeline toward Türkiye/Europe); (c) concrete step — ABSENT: no MOU/tender/FEED/EPC/permit/FID for the export pipeline. Sources: karamshaar.com AGP/Syria analysis (Jan 2026, explicitly frames Akkas→AGP as historical/aspirational, halted by war, only under renewed post-Assad discussion) and en.wikipedia Arab_Gas_Pipeline (2004 four-country framework to link AGP with Iraq's grid) — both URL-verified (200 + expected substring). Corroborated independently by Energy Intelligence and OilPrice coverage of the Akkas field (domestic-supply focus; SLB drilling started Jan 2026). Note the recent concrete Iraq–Syria cross-border activity is a different project and a different commodity: the Kirkuk–Baniyas OIL pipeline revival (oil, not gas). Confidence: findings well-supported by 2+ independent English sources, but the pipeline itself remains rumor/aspiration — low tier as an early-stage monitor item. Recommend keeping on the watchlist; revisit if a cross-border gas MOU/tender/EPC or a formal Iraq–Syria gas-transit agreement is signed.
